vt_1_west_side.blurb: West Side is the western end of Bolton Dome, a historic cliff in the Bolton area of northern Vermont. A dozen lines are spread across a mix of trad and bolted sport, plus a top-rope and a single boulder problem. Grades start as low as 5.2 and run to 5.11, with a small cluster at 5.10, so it suits both newer leaders and people looking for a hard sport pitch. The end of the cliff sits among trees, which makes it a comfortable place to start a day, and the walk in from the road is short.

vt_3_railroad_yard.blurb: Railroad Yard is a small sector on Bolton Dome in northern Vermont, a short way to the right of the Bat Wall. It mixes a few older crack climbs with newer bolted lines, and a dozen routes are known here: seven sport and five trad. Grades run from 5.4 up to 5.10, and half of the routes sit at 5.10, so there is a lot for solid intermediates but only a handful of easier options. Several lines go beyond one pitch, which gives it a bit more of an adventure feel than a typical roadside wall.

vt_5_main_wall.blurb: Main Wall is the tallest section of Bolton Dome, on the south-facing side of the cliff above the Interstate corridor in northern Vermont. It holds some of the oldest climbing at the dome alongside newer bolted additions. Of twelve routes, nine are sport, two are trad and one is aid. The difficulty is aimed at strong climbers: most lines fall between 5.11 and 5.12, with one at 5.13 and just a pair of easier ones near 5.9 and 5.10. A large scoop in the wall serves as a landmark when you arrive.

vt_bone_doctor_the.blurb: The Bone Doctor is a boulder in the cluster of blocks behind the visitor center at the top of Smugglers' Notch, Vermont, and it is the most conspicuous one in the lot. Twelve problems, all bouldering, run from around V4 through to V13, so it leans toward strong climbers with a long overhanging traverse, steep roof moves and a few of the hardest lines in the state. A few easier problems sit on the left side. Chalk marks the popular holds, and the boulder is clearly visible from the parking area.

vt_pisgah_south_trail_moraine.blurb: This is a small bouldering zone beside the south trail up Mount Pisgah in the Northeast Kingdom of Vermont. Glacial deposits left granite blocks scattered through hardwood forest, and about a dozen problems have been climbed on them. Most are short and sit at the easy to moderate end, from VB through V5, with a single harder problem near V7. The blocks are often damp and mossy, and the forest setting is quiet and intimate rather than a crowded circuit, with plenty of unclimbed rock still along the trail.

vt_b_upper_tier_left_end.blurb: Upper Tier - Left End is the southern end of the Upper West cliff in Bolton, Vermont, found by working around the left side of the big boulder pile on the walk up. All twelve routes are bolted sport lines in a tight grade band: two at 5.8, one at 5.9 and nine at 5.10. A dark face that can stay damp sits beside a ledge with several short lines, making this a good stop for climbers working through the 5.8 to 5.10 range on single pitches.

vt_quartz_crack_face.blurb: Quartz Crack Face is a big, steep wall that towers over the main parking area at the top of Smugglers' Notch in Vermont, with huge roofs near the top. It is mainly a trad face: ten of its twelve lines are trad and two are sport. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.12, with most clustered around 5.9 and a couple of harder lines at the top end. Protection is generally decent, though a few easy stretches are run out, and many popular lines have bolted rappel stations. Don't underestimate the lower grades.
